context_requirements: Cells must express CDC42 and its downstream effectors (PAK1, IQGAP1, WASP/WAVE) for the specific mechanism to engage.
Adherent, motile cells with active actin-cytoskeletal and adhesion signaling are more likely to show early immediate-early gene and cytoskeletal transcriptional changes.
Proliferation-dependent late effects require cells with intact cell-cycle machinery and, for apoptosis, permissive TP53 or mitochondrial priming.
Lines with high efflux or low CDC42-pathway dependence may show little or no response.
falsifiers: No change in CDC42-pathway immediate-early genes (EGR1, FOS, JUN, ZFP36) at 6 h in any line.
No reduction in proliferation or cell-cycle genes (CCNA2, CCNB1, CDK1, AURKA) at 24 h in responsive lines.
A response pattern indistinguishable from generic stress (HSPA1A, DNAJB1, HMOX1) without cytoskeletal or adhesion gene changes.
Strong upregulation of CDC42 or its effectors at 6 h, which would argue against effective GTPase inhibition.
Equal magnitude across all nine lines, which would suggest a non-specific cytotoxic rather than a CDC42-dependent mechanism.

evidence.supports: GTPase inhibition (Drp1) reduces proliferation and increases apoptosis in vascular cells, supporting antiproliferative/apoptotic consequences of GTPase inhibitors.
Dynamin 2 GTPase inhibition (dynasore) increases apoptosis and modulates cell-cycle progression in triple-negative breast cancer cells.
OPA1 GTPase inhibition promotes cytochrome c release and apoptosis, supporting apoptosis as a downstream consequence of GTPase inhibition.
RAC1 GTPase inhibition resensitizes resistant ovarian carcinoma cells, linking GTPase inhibition to DNA-damage/apoptotic stress responses.
GTPase inhibitor GGTI-298 inhibits proliferation, migration and induces G1 arrest and apoptosis in endometrial cancer cells.
